A 55-year-old male presents to his physician with complaints of not feeling well. He reports
experiencing nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, muscle cramps, a runny nose, and generalized aches and

pains in his muscles and joints since yesterday. His medical history includes obesity, chronic
pulmonary disease, lower back pain, and fibromyalgia. His current medications are varenicline,
oxycodone, and an albuterol inhaler. He requests antibiotics and a refill of his prescriptions during this
visit. He works at a public school and had a similar complaint a week ago, during which his medications
were refilled. Several of his coworkers have presented with similar complaints recently and were
advised conservative management. His vital signs are: temperature 98.5°F (37.1°C), blood pressure
104/83 mmHg, pulse 88/min, respirations 19/min, and oxygen saturation 98% on room air. What is the
most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Acetaminophen for symptomatic
relief (B) Methadone (C) Referral to pain management (D) Tapering of oxycodone (E) Initiation of
antibiotics (F) Supportive therapy (G) Naloxone administration (H) Oseltamivir (I) Intravenous fluids for
dehydration (J) Buprenorphine-naloxone
 A. Supportive therapy
B. Buprenorphine-naloxone
C. Methadone
D. Intravenous fluids for dehydration
